content.user_title: Control Chrome for Testing and Debugging
content.value_statement: Browser tasks often require real interaction and diagnostics that simple HTTP requests cannot provide. This skill controls Chrome through a focused command-line workflow.
actual_capabilities: Navigate web pages in a Chrome browser session.
Capture page snapshots, screenshots, and visible content.
Click controls and fill forms during interactive flows.
Run JavaScript and inspect console or network activity.
Audit website performance through the CLI.
limitations: Requires an environment that can run npx and Chrome.
Current command details are available only through the CLI help.
Browser interactions can change page state or submit data.
Simple HTTP retrieval is better handled with fetch or curl.

use_cases.title: Debug a Web Page
use_cases.description: Reproduce a page issue, then inspect console messages and network activity.

use_cases.title: Test an Interactive Flow
use_cases.description: Navigate a site, click controls, fill forms, and verify visible results.

use_cases.title: Review Page Performance
use_cases.description: Open a target page, run a performance audit, and summarize observed concerns.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect a Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Open [URL], capture the page state, and summarize the main visible content. Do not interact with forms.

prompt_templates.title: Check Browser Errors
prompt_templates.prompt: Open [URL], reproduce [issue], and inspect console and network activity. Report errors with the action that triggered each one.

prompt_templates.title: Test a Form Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Test the [flow] on [URL] using [test data]. Stop before any irreversible submission and report each observed result.

prompt_templates.title: Audit and Compare Performance
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit performance for [page A] and [page B] under equivalent conditions. Compare findings and prioritize the most important improvements.

output_examples.input: Open the product page and summarize its visible state.
output: The page loaded with a product title, price, image gallery, and purchase controls.

output_examples.input: Reproduce the failed search and inspect browser diagnostics.
output: The search request failed after submission.
The console reported a related client error, and the network request returned an unsuccessful response.

output_examples.input: Audit the page performance and list priorities.
output: The audit identified slow initial rendering and delayed asset loading.
Prioritize the largest blocking resources before lower-impact changes.

best_practices: Read the current CLI help before selecting commands or flags.
Use test accounts and scoped data for interactive workflows.
Confirm targets and expected side effects before submitting forms or changing page state.
anti_patterns: Do not launch a browser when a simple HTTP request provides the needed result.
Do not execute CLI-suggested commands without validating their arguments.
Do not perform sensitive or irreversible production actions without explicit approval.

faq.question: Does this skill require a global installation?
faq.answer: No. The skill invokes chrome-devtools-axi through npx.

faq.question: What browser tasks can it perform?
faq.answer: It can navigate, capture page state, click controls, fill forms, run JavaScript, and take screenshots.

faq.question: Can it help debug website errors?
faq.answer: Yes. It can inspect browser console messages and network activity while reproducing a problem.

faq.question: Can it test form workflows?
faq.answer: Yes. It can enter values, activate controls, and observe the resulting page state.

faq.question: When should I avoid this skill?
faq.answer: Avoid it when fetch or curl can retrieve the required information without browser interaction.

faq.question: Where are current commands and flags documented?
faq.answer: Use the CLI help for current commands, flags, environment variables, and contextual next steps.
